entities.summary: Jean Drapeau was a Canadian politician who served as mayor of Montreal for 2 non-consecutive terms from 1954 to 1957 and from 1960 to 1986. Major accomplishments of the Drapeau Administration include the development of the Montreal Metro entirely underground mass transit subway system running on 'whisper quiet' rubber wheels, a successful international exposition Expo 67 as well as the construction of a major performing arts centre, the Place des Arts. Drapeau also secured the hosting of the 1976 Summer Olympics and was instrumental in building the Olympic Stadium and then world's tallest inclined tower.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jean Drapeau's administration played a pivotal role in shaping Montreal and Quebec's modern identity through his vision for Expo 67, which brought international attention to Canada. His legacy also includes the development of Montreal's underground metro system and the construction of the Olympic Stadium.
